channel.title: QuietWealth.news
channel.description: Patient, practical investing and wealth-building coverage — crypto, tokenized assets, real estate, dividend investing, tax strategy, and retirement.

item.title: The 1099-K Threshold Is Back to $20,000. Here's What That Means for Your Side Hustle.
item.description: The IRS confirmed in late 2025 that the 1099-K reporting threshold reverts to $20,000 and 200 transactions, undoing a 2021 rule change that caused years of confusion for gig and marketplace sellers. Here's what actually changed, and why your tax obligation on that income never depended on the form in the first place.

item.title: Custodial Roth IRA: How to Invest Your Kid's First Paycheck Tax-Free
item.description: A custodial Roth IRA lets a child with earned income invest for decades of tax-free growth, contribution-matched by a parent up to the child's actual earnings. Here's the earned-income rule that makes or breaks the account, the 2026 contribution limits, who controls the money and when that changes, and where this fits alongside a 529 or a UTMA account.

item.title: Family Office 101: What They Are, and Who Actually Needs One
item.description: Over 8,000 single-family offices now manage roughly $5.5 trillion in assets worldwide, and multi-family offices have opened a version of this service to families well below the ultra-wealthy tier. Here's what a family office actually does day to day, the net worth thresholds where single- and multi-family versions each start to make financial sense, what they cost, and why the underlying principles apply at any net worth even when the structure itself doesn't.

item.title: The Scam Series, Part 2: When the Voice on the Phone Is a Perfect Fake
item.description: The FBI logged $893 million in AI-related scam losses in 2025, with $352 million hitting adults 60 and older. Part 2 of our scam series covers how AI voice cloning turned the old grandparent scam into something that can fool the people who know that voice best — and the one habit that stops it cold.

item.title: Tax-Loss Harvesting: The Year-End Move Worth Understanding Before December 31
item.description: Tax-loss harvesting can offset up to $3,000 of ordinary income a year, with unlimited carryforward into future years — but the wash-sale rule, dividend reinvestment, and multi-account coordination are where careful investors still make expensive mistakes. Here's the mechanics, the 2026 capital gains brackets, and the honest limits of the strategy.

item.title: Trusts 101: Revocable vs. Irrevocable, and When a Will Isn't Enough
item.description: With the federal estate tax exemption permanently set at $15 million per person for 2026, most families' real motivation for a trust isn't estate-tax avoidance. Here's what revocable and irrevocable trusts each actually do, what they cost, the funding mistake that renders a trust worthless, and an honest guide to when a will and updated beneficiary designations are enough on their own.

item.title: UTMA and UGMA Accounts, Explained: The Custodial Account Most Parents Get Wrong
item.description: UTMA and UGMA custodial accounts let a family gift assets to a child with no restrictions on how the money is eventually used — but they come with a kiddie-tax bite, a hard handoff of full control at 18 or 21, and a financial-aid penalty roughly four times steeper than a 529 plan's. Here's how the two differ, the 2026 tax figures, and where this account actually fits.

item.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs Just Posted Their Fattest 2026 Inflow Day. That Is a Plumbing Story, Not a Signal to Chase.
item.description: Nearly $1 billion of creations on Monday coincided with bitcoin reclaiming levels not seen in months — as oil slid and risk appetite firmed. For patient investors, the useful questions are about sleeve size, dollar-cost averaging, and what lower energy prices imply for inflation and the Fed path — not whether to leverage the next candle.

item.title: Existing-Home Sales Dipped in August. Affordability Quietly Got Better Anyway.
item.description: NAR's August existing-home sales report shows a 2% monthly decline, but inventory climbed to its highest level in more than a decade and the national affordability index improved year-over-year. Here's what the full data set says that the sales headline alone doesn't.

item.title: Mr. Wonderful's Real Investing Rulebook Isn't From Shark Tank. It's From His Mother.
item.description: Kevin O'Leary's public persona runs on blunt one-liners. His actual investing discipline traces to two real, verifiable threads: a signal-to-noise focus lesson he credits to Steve Jobs, and a set of rules his mother followed for 55 years that he still uses for his family trust today.

item.title: Meta's Muse AI Agent Is Rewriting Wall Street's Monetization Thesis. You Probably Already Own the Stock.
item.description: Analysts are modeling consumer AI subscriptions as a new earnings engine inside Meta. For index investors, that is a reminder that mega-cap cash-flow optionality compounds quietly — without requiring a launch-day chase of the app, the options chain, or the narrative.

item.title: The 2027 Social Security COLA Estimate: What to Do (and Not Do) With It Right Now
item.description: Early estimates from AARP and the Senior Citizens League put the 2027 Social Security cost-of-living adjustment in the mid-3% range, with the official figure due October 14. Here's what actually drives the number, why it can still move, and how to plan around it without overreacting to a preview.

item.title: The Fed Just Hiked, Not Cut: What It Means for Your Mortgage
item.description: The September 2026 FOMC meeting raised rates to 3.75%-4.00%, reversing the expected cutting cycle. 30-year mortgage rates jumped to a one-year high near 6.97%. Here's what actually changed, and what didn't.

item.title: Fractional Real Estate Investing: What $100 Actually Buys You
item.description: Platforms like Arrived and Ark7 let you buy a slice of a rental property for $100. Here's what that share actually gets you — and the fees, illiquidity, and platform risk the marketing doesn't lead with.

item.title: The "Passive Income" Myth: What Most of These Income Streams Actually Require
item.description: Rental property, dividend investing, content creation, staking — almost everything marketed as passive income requires real upfront work, capital, or ongoing attention. Here's an honest accounting.

item.title: The Scam Series, Part 1: How to Spot Phishing Before It Costs You
item.description: Americans reported a record $15.9 billion in fraud losses in 2025, and older adults are being targeted more than ever. Part 1 of our scam series covers the phishing, smishing, and vishing basics everyone still falls for.

item.title: 529 or Brokerage Account? Two Ways to Start Investing for Your Kid
item.description: A 529 plan is built for college. A custodial brokerage account is built for anything. Here's the real tradeoff — tax breaks, control, and what happens if the money isn't for tuition.

item.title: 7 Dividend Stocks Worth Putting on Your Watchlist
item.description: Not a buy list — a research list. Seven long-tenured dividend payers across healthcare, staples, energy, real estate, and industrials, and the questions to ask before you ever place an order.

item.title: Backdoor Roth IRA, Explained Without the Jargon
item.description: If your income is too high to contribute to a Roth IRA directly, the backdoor Roth is the legal workaround high earners use. Here's how it actually works, and the one rule that trips people up.

item.title: Bitcoin Dollar-Cost Averaging: The Boring Way to Own Crypto
item.description: Spot bitcoin ETFs made recurring, small bitcoin purchases as easy as buying an index fund. Here's how DCA works, why it exists, and what it doesn't solve.

item.title: The Case for Boring Blue Chips in 2026
item.description: The S&P 500's top holdings are more concentrated than they've been in decades. Here's the case for the unglamorous, decades-old blue chips sitting outside that concentration.

item.title: Donating Appreciated Assets: The Tax Move Most People Never Make
item.description: Selling appreciated stock to donate the cash triggers capital gains tax you didn't have to pay. Donating the asset directly avoids it entirely — and most people who give to charity never do it.

item.title: Estate Planning Basics Everyone Under 40 Skips (and Shouldn't)
item.description: 56% of Americans still have no estate plan in 2026. Here's what a basic estate plan actually requires — and why it has nothing to do with how much money you have.

item.title: Where American Retirees Are Actually Moving in 2026: Portugal, Panama, and the New Expat Map
item.description: Portugal's retirement visa requires just €920 a month in income. Panama's requires $1,000 and comes with statutory discounts on almost everything. A grounded look at where retirees are actually going in 2026.

item.title: Farmland as an Asset Class: What the Data Actually Shows
item.description: Farmland has a decades-long track record of low correlation with stocks and bonds — but the cash yields are modest and the minimums are steep. A grounded look at what farmland investing actually offers.

item.title: House Hacking: How to Get Your Housing Costs to (Almost) Zero
item.description: FHA loans allow 3.5% down on owner-occupied 2-4 unit properties — and rental income from the other units can cover most or all of the mortgage. Here's how house hacking actually works.

item.title: How to Read a Balance Sheet in Five Minutes
item.description: Assets, liabilities, and equity — the three numbers that make up every balance sheet, and the handful of ratios that tell you whether a company is actually healthy.

item.title: The HSA: The Most Underrated Retirement Account Nobody Maxes Out
item.description: A Health Savings Account is the only account with a triple tax advantage — and most people who have one treat it like a debit card instead of a retirement account. Here's the case for maxing it out.

item.title: Index vs. Active: What Decades of Data Actually Say
item.description: Year after year, the majority of active large-cap fund managers underperform the S&P 500 over long horizons. Here's what the SPIVA data actually shows, and where active management still earns its fee.

item.title: Is Flipping Houses Still Worth It? Run These Numbers Before You Buy
item.description: Flip margins ticked up in Q1 2026 after seven straight quarters of decline — but they're still below last year. Here's the actual math to run before you buy a flip.
